stem: An inpatient Massachusetts hospice has 18 licensed beds. Under the acute-use ADD circular, its caps are 100 Schedule II-V analgesic units, 60 Schedule II-V sedative/anticonvulsant units, and 50 Schedule VI ancillary units. Which proposed category totals comply? Select all that apply.

choices.text: 101 Schedule II-V analgesic units because one extra unit may be borrowed from the ancillary category
70 Schedule II-V sedative units because the hospice has fewer than 21 beds
100 units of approved morphine/other Schedule II-V analgesic stock in the analgesic category
60 units of approved lorazepam/other Schedule II-V sedative stock in the sedative category
40 units of an approved Schedule VI ancillary antiemetic in the ancillary category

explanation.core_reasoning: Hospice acute-use limits are separate category caps; unused capacity in one category does not increase another category's limit.

choice_analysis.C: That is at the 100-unit analgesic cap.

related_facts: The hospice need not stock each maximum.
explanation.mpje_trap: Treating the three category maxima as one fungible pool.

reasoning_steps: Map each drug category to its separate cap
Reject shifting unused capacity across categories
